newsitem.title: GERMANY: German pharmacies post stronger 10-month sales.
newsitem.headline: German pharmacies post stronger 10-month sales.

text.p: German pharmacies posted a 7.8 percent rise in sales in the first 10 months of the year, but an industry association predicted this level could fall off in the last two months, pulling down the annual rate.

The industry association Verband Forschender Arzneimittelhersteller (VFA) forecast that in light of a sharp drop in sales in November, the rise in pharmacy sales for the entire year 1996 could be below six percent.
In the first 10 months of the year, German pharmacies sold 21 billion marks worth of products, the group said at a news conference.
Looking ahead, nearly 40 percent of the association's members expect softer sales next year, as Germany's medication budgets for physicians are designed to curb prescriptions.
But exports could help boost growth, the association said. This year the group already sees exports topping last year's 15.2 billion mark sales.
